CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 1 OF 20




                       BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF OKLAHOMA

        IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION
        OF OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC
        COMPANY FOR AN ORDER OF THE
        COMMISSION APPROVING ITS NEW
        EXTRA LARGE LOAD TARIFF AND
        TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE                          CAUSE NO. PUD2026-000046
        FOR EXTRA LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS
        AND A REGULATORY ASSET TO
        RECOVER COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH
        PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION SOFTWARE


          OKLAHOMA INDUSTRIAL ENERGY CONSUMERS' OBJECTIONS TO CERTAIN
             OF OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY'S DATA REQUESTS
                 Oklahoma Industrial Energy Consumers ("OIEC"), objects to Data Requests Nos. 1-3, 1-

         4, and 1-6 submitted by Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company ("OG&E") to OIEC, which Data

         Requests are set forth on Exhibit "A" attached hereto. In support thereof, OIEC states as follows:

                 1.        OIEC objects to Data Requests Nos. OGE-OIEC 1-3 and 1-4 because they seek

         information from or about individual members of OIEC.

                            (a)   Such information is neither relevant nor likely to lead to the discovery of

         admissible evidence.

                            (b)   The information sought is confidential and/or proprietary information.

                            (c)   The information requested in Data Requests Nos. 1-3 and 1-4 is not within

         OIEC's possession, custody or control. OIEC's members do not furnish such information to OIEC

         and OIEC has no authority or right to compel its members to provide such information. There is

         no authority to seek discovery of information that is not in possession of OIEC and that has not

         been relied upon in this proceeding.

                 The individual members are not parties to this proceeding. Requiring OIEC to provide

        information that is not relevant, not within its possession, custody or control, and/or that is



        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 20
                                                               OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                        Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                      Page 2 of 11


         confidential would chill participation in regulatory proceedings by voluntary associations and

         trade associations, such as OIEC, as it would also undermine their First and Fourteenth

         Amendment Associational rights.

                 2.        The Commission has previously determined that data requests pertaining to

         OIEC's members were not appropriate. See Order No. 501834, entered in Cause PUD 200200754,

         a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit "B".

                 3.        OIEC objects to Data Request No. 1-6 to the extent it seeks information as to the

         law and/or to require OIEC to provide an opinion as to the law and legal issues.

                                        ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

         I.      THIS PROCEEDING DOES NOT INVOLVE OIEC'S INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS
                 AND DISCOVERY REQUESTS RELATING TO THOSE MEMBERS ARE NOT
                 PROPER.

                 OIEC is an unincorporated association consisting of a diverse group of industrial

         consumers. It represents its members in promoting and protecting the membership's collective

        interests in matters concerning government regulation affecting electric and natural gas issues.

        The value of participation of voluntary associations in various proceedings has been recognized

        by the courts. See, e.g., International Union, United Automobile Workers, etc. v. Brock, 477 U.S.

        274, 289 (1986) ("[T]he interest and expertise of this plaintiff... assure that concrete adverseness

        which sharpens the presentation of issues upon which the court so largely depends for

        illumination of difficult . . . questions.") (internal quotations and citations omitted). Many of

        OIEC's members are in competition with each other and they do not provide confidential or

        proprietary information to OIEC and OIEC has no authority or right to acquire such information

        from its members. Requiring OIEC to provide information that is not relevant or that is



        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 20
                                                                  OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                           Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                         Page 3 of 11


         confidential or competitively sensitive information about its members when their association

         intervenes in a Commission proceeding will undermine the very reason for their association with

         OIEC, and have a chilling effect on their First and Fourteenth Amendment associational rights.

         See Roberts v. United States Jaycees, 468 U.S. 609, 622 (1984) ("[W]e have long understood as

         implicit in the right to engage in activities protected by the First Amendment a corresponding right

         to associate with others in pursuit of a wide variety of political, social, economic, educational,

         religious, and cultural ends"); National Commodity & Barter Ass 'n v. Archer, 31 F.3d 1521, 1528

         (10th Cir. 1994) ("It is beyond debate that freedom to engage in association ... is an inseparable

         aspect of the liberty assured by the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. ... The

         Supreme Court declared this right to be protected against both intentional and incidental

         infringement.").1

                 The information sought by OG&E is not relevant to this proceeding. Data Requests Nos.

         1-3 and 1-4 seek information about individual OIEC members' maximum demand on OG&E's

         system, whether individual members anticipate adding load, and whether individual members

        would then become subject to OG&E's proposed XLPL Tariff. OIEC has intervened in this cause

         for purposes of participating in a determination of OG&E's request to approve its new Extra Large

        Load Tariff and terms and conditions of service for extra-large load customers. The current or

         future potential business plans of OIEC's members is not relevant to the Commission's



        1 As stated in International Union, 477 U.S. at 290:
                    [T[he doctrine of associational standing recognizes that the primary reason people
                    join an organization is often to create an effective vehicle for vindicating interests
                    that they share with others. "The only practical judicial policy when people pool
                    their capital, their interests, or their activities under a name and form that will
                    identify collective interests, often is to permit the association or corporation in a
                    single case to vindicate the interests of all." (citations omitted).


        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 4 OF 20
                                                                   OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                            Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 11



         determination of this cause.

                 This Commission has previously found that data requests seeking information about

         OIEC's members in a proceeding involving a public utility's rates and practices were improper.

        See Order attached hereto as Exhibit "B". Similarly, the Kansas Public Utility Commission has

        held that an association was not required to produce documents relating to its members' practices

        because such information is irrelevant where the proceeding is about a regulated utility's practices,

        rather than about the unregulated members' practices. See Matter of Investigation of Actions of

         Western Resources, Inc. to Separate its Jurisdictional Electric Public Utility Business from its

         Unregulated Businesses, Docket No. 01-WSRE-949-GIE, 2002 Kan. PUC LEXIS 629 (Kan.

        P.U.C. June 6, 2002). In the latter cause, the Kansas Commission, in determining that the Kansas

        Industrial Consumers ("KIC") were not required to produce information about its members in

        response to an electric utility's data requests, stated:

                            This proceeding is not about KIC, the corporate structures of the
                            companies comprising KIC or that of their subsidiaries, affiliates
                            or members. Nor is the proceeding about the accounting and
                            financial practices of the companies comprising KIC or the
                            compensation paid by them to their executives. Rather, this
                            proceeding is about the financial health of a KCC jurisdictional
                            utility and its affiliate relations. Moreover, the KIC companies are
                            not public utilities that are obligated to provide sufficient and
                            efficient electric service at just and reasonable rates established by
                            the Commission. Any inference that can be drawn from a
                            comparison with KIC companies would have weak probative
                            value, if any.
        Id. at *9-10. See also 12 O.S. § 2401, which defines "relevant evidence" as "evidence having any

        tendency to make the existence of any fact in consequence to the determination of the action more

        probable or less probable than it would be without the evidence." See also Quinn v. Tulsa, 1989

        OK 112, 777 P.2d 1331, 1342 ("the requirement. . . that the material sought in discovery be


        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 5 OF 20
                                                               OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                        Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                      Page 5 of 11


         'relevant' should be firmly applied, and the district courts should not neglect their power to restrict

        discovery where 'justice requires [protection for] a party or a person from annoyance,

        embarrassment, oppression, or undue burden or expense. . . .'"); Nitzel v. Jackson, 1994 OK 49,

         879 P.2d 1222, 1223 n. 1 (in holding that plaintiffs' employment records were irrelevant and not

         subject to discovery, court stated that "[d]iscovery is not without limitation. It must lead or tend to

        lead to relevant evidence. Fishing expeditions are not allowed upon the suggestion that something

        may or might be discovered... .").

                 Finally, OIEC cannot be compelled to produce information that is not within its

        possession, custody or control. By way of analogy, under the Oklahoma Discovery Code a party

        is not required to produce documents that are not within its "possession, custody or control." 12

        O.S. § 3234(A)(1). Thus, it has been held that a party, which was an employee of the City of

        Norman, could not be required to produce his police department personnel file, which was not

        available to him because such documents were not in his possession, custody or control. See

        Newell v. Nash, 1994 OK CIV APP 143, 889 P.2d 345, 348. Under the similar provisions of the

        federal discovery rules, the Tenth Circuit has stated:

                            [A] party moving for an order requiring production of documents
                            from another party . . . "is charged with establishing that the
                            desired documents, etc., designated in the motion for production
                            are in the possession, custody or control of the party to whom the
                            motion is directed, and that a 'party may not be compelled to
                            produce papers or things which are not in his possession, custody,
                            or control'.."
         United States v. 25.02 Acres ofLand, 495 F.2d 1398, 1402 (10th Cir. 1974), quoting Norman v.

        Young, 422 F.2d 470, 472, 473 (10th Cir. 1970).

                 The above rules have been applied in cases involving associations. For example, in In re



        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 6 OF 20
                                                                  OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                           Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                         Page 6 of 11



         Regulatory Frameworks for Local Exchange Carriers, 55 Cal. Pub. Util. Comm'n 2d 672 (Cal.

         P.U.C. Aug. 3, 1994), the California Cable Television Association (CCTA) appealed a ruling of

         an ALJ, granting Pacific Bell's motion to compel the CCTA to answer a data request that would

         require the CCTA to obtain documents and information from its members. The California Public

         Utilities Commission overturned the ALJ's decision, ruling:

                            We conclude that the Commission cannot compel an association to
                            require its individual members to answer data requests. Our
                            reasoning for that is rather straightforward. One of the principal
                            purposes of discovery is to enable the discovering party to obtain
                            evidence from one's adversary who has control of the information
                            in question, (citations omitted) If information is being sought from
                            individual members, it is unlikely that the association possesses or
                            has control over that sort of information.

         Id.

                  In University of Texas v. Vratil, 96 F.3d 1337 (10th Cir. 1996), the National Collegiate

         Athletic Association (NCAA) was sued for alleged violations of federal antitrust statutes. The

         district court ruled that the NCAA's members were the "real parties in interest," and ordered each

         member to respond directly to interrogatories propounded to the NCAA. The Tenth Circuit issued

         a writ of prohibition, holding that the members were not parties and persons who were not parties

         could not be required to answer interrogatories. The court stated:

                            The district court erred in characterizing the unserved, nonparty
                            petitioners as "real parties in interest" for discovery purposes, and
                            acted without jurisdiction in ordering them to respond to
                            interrogatories propounded under Rule 33. Rule 17(b)(1), which
                            provides for suit against an unincorporated association "for the
                            purpose of enforcing for or against it a substantive right," recognizes
                            the NCAA as the procedural party defendant before the court. This
                            party status clearly extends to party discovery.

         Id. at 1340.



         23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 7 OF 20
                                                                 OIEC’s Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                          Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                        Page 7 of 11


                 OIEC, rather than its members, is a party to this proceeding. OIEC properly intervened in

        these proceedings under Okla. Const, art. 9, § 20 and the Commission's rules. See, e.g., State ex

        rel. Henry v. Southwestern Bell Tel. Co., 1991 OK 134, 825 P.2d 1305, 1310 (American

        Association of Retired Persons intervened in a rate proceeding brought by Commission's staff;

        court held that the Association had standing to appeal because its "membership is composed of

        individuals who presumably are ratepayers"). See also Oklahoma State AFL-CIO v. State Board

        for Property & Casualty Rates, 1970 OK 3, 463 P.2d 693, 694; Oklahoma State Senate v. State

        Boardfor Property & Casualty Rates, 2000 OK 69, 11 P.3d 1242, 1245. Importantly, no objection

        to OIEC's intervention was made by OG&E.

                 The Oklahoma Supreme Court, as well as the United States Supreme Court, have

         recognized that even when an association brings a lawsuit in its representational capacity, and

         where prospective relief is sought, such as injunctive or declaratory relief (as opposed to

         damages), it is not anticipated that the individual members will participate in the discovery or

         trial of the lawsuit. See, e.g., Oklahoma Public Employees Ass 'n v. Oklahoma Dep't of Central

         Services, Inc., 2002 OK 71, 55 P.3d 1072, 1077; Hunt v. Washington State Apple Advertising

         Comm ‘n, 432 U.S. 333, 343 (1977) (". . . an association has standing to bring suit on behalf of

         its members when: .. . neither the claim asserted nor the relief requested requires the participation of

         individual members in the lawsuit").2 The present cause is not a lawsuit. Instead, it is a proceeding to


         2 In Hunt, the Court further stated:
                     "[W]hether an association has standing to invoke the court's remedial powers on
                     behalf of its members depends in substantial measure on the nature of the relief
                     sought. If in a proper case the association seeks a declaration, injunction, or some
                     other form of prospective relief, it can reasonably be supposed that the remedy, if
                     granted, will inure to the benefit of those members of the association actually
                     injured. Indeed, in all cases in which we have expressly recognized standing in
                     associations to represent their members, the relief sought has been of this kind."

        23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 8 OF 20
                                                               OIEC's Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                        Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                      Page 8 of 11


          approve or disapprove of OG&E's proposed Extra Large Load Tariff in which the Commission is to

          examine OG&E's proposal and its practices in connection therewith. OIEC's participation in this case

          is germane to OIEC's purpose, which is to promote and protect its members' interest in the regulation

          and rates of public utilities that provide electric power and natural gas. Therefore, OIEC's members

          are not the real parties in interest and cannot be compelled, through Data Requests propounded on

          OIEC, to provide information.

                  Further, the information sought by OIEC is not only irrelevant, it is also the confidential

          and proprietary information of OIEC's individual members, many of whom are in competition

          with each other. Under similar circumstances, another agency has ruled that an association cannot

         be compelled to provide information pertaining to its members. In Pacific Gas Transmission Co.,

          70 F.E.R.C. 1 61,023, 1995 FERC LEXIS 52 (Jan. 13, 1995), the Federal Energy Regulatory

          Commission ("FERC") vacated an order of the ALJ that required the Canadian Association of

          Petroleum Producers ("CAPP") to respond to data requests requesting documents and information

         pertaining to CAPP's members in a rate proceeding, in which CAPP had intervened. The CAPP

         was an incorporated industry trade association "charged with presenting the consensus view of

          its members and providing other member services." It was argued that the information sought

         was relevant to test the accuracy of the expert testimony presented by CAPP. The court held that

         this reason was insufficient because the documents and information sought were not relied upon

         by the expert. The Commission, in denying the requested production of documents and

         information, further stated:

                            In addition, the All does not appear to have considered the


         432 U.S. at 343, quoting Warth v. Seldin, 422 U.S. 490, 515 (1975).


         23145898.1:620435.01539
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 54 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/30/2026 - PAGE 9 OF 20
                                                              OIEC’s Objection to Certain of OG&E's Data Requests
                                                                                       Cause No. PUD2026-000046
                                                                                                     Page 9 of 11

                           competitive relationship of the parties. The Commission has stated
                           that where competitors are involved in a discovery dispute, the
                           ALJ must exercise increased caution to avoid unnecessary
                           disclosure.

         Id., 70 F.E.R.C. at 61,085.

         II.               Data Request No. 1-6 Improperly Seeks Information as to the Law and Legal
                           Opinions.

                 OIEC objects to Data Request No. 1-6 to the extent that it seeks disclosure of the law and

         legal opinions and information regarding a legal conclusion. Specifically, OG&E's Data Request

         No. 1-6 asks, "Does OIEC contend that the Commission lacks authority under 17 § 152 and its

         general ratemaking power to establish a rate class for any 75 MW customer independent of HB

         2992?" and, if so, to "identify the authority." See Data Request OGE-OIEC 1-6. This data request

         seeks information that is outside the scope of permissible discovery. The purpose of discovery is

         to promote disclosure of the relevant facts. See State ex rel. Protective Health Services v. Billings

         Fairchild Center, Inc., 2007 OK CIV APP 24, 158 P.3d 484, 489 ("The aim of these liberal

         discovery rules is to make a trial less a game of blind man's bluff and more a fair contest with the

         basic issues and facts disclosed to the fullest practicable extent.") (internal quotation marks and

         citations omitted); Boswell v. Schultz, 2007 OK 94, 175 P.3d 390, 395 ("The purpose of modern

         discovery practice and procedure is to promote the discovery of the true facts and circumstances

         of the controversy . . . ."). Moreover, Data Request 1-6 is vague. As written, the request asks if

         OIEC denies the existence of certain authority and, if it does, to identify the authority OIEC

         denies exists. This is a nonsensical request.




        23145898.1:620435.01539

                                                                                                  Page 10 of 11

                                                  CONCLUSION

                   For the above reasons, OIEC respectfully requests that the Commission enter an order

         determining that OIEC is not required to respond to OG&E's Data Requests Nos. 1-3, 1-4, and 1-

         6.

           or "Responding Party") by and through its counsel of record. OG&E requests that OIEC respond

           preparing the response, by delivering the answers and all requested documents and materials to

           Orders. Responding Party is requested to provide a complete copy of all responses or objections

                                         INSTRUCTIONS


           1.    Reproduce the data requests being responded to before the response.
           2.    Responses to any and all data requests that are contained herein or that may be served later
                  should be supplied to OG&E as soon as they become available to Responding Party. That
                  is, Responding Party should not hold answers to any requests for which it does have data,
                  documents, etc., until responses to any or all other requests are compiled.
           3.    The response to each data request should be made by a person competent to testify
                  concerning the response and all documents and exhibits produced as part of the response.
                  With respect to each request, please state the name(s) and title(s) of the person or persons
                  responsible for preparing the responses and date on which each question was answered.
           4.     Where information requested is not available in the precise form described in the question
                  or is not available for all years (or other periods of classification) indicated in a series of
                  years (or other periods of classification), please provide all information with respect to the
                  subject matter of the question that can be identified in your, or any affiliated entity's, work
                  papers and files or all such information that is otherwise available.
           Case No. PUD2026-000046                                                                   Page 2 of 7
           OG&E's First Set of Data Requests
           OGE-OIEC-1

           5.      These data requests and interrogatories shall be deemed to be continuing in nature and
                   Responding Party is requested to supplement its responses as necessary. Responding Party
                   is requested to change, supplement and correct its answers to conform to all information as
                   it becomes available, including the substitution of actual data for estimated data.
                   Responses to requests for information covering a period not entirely in the past (or for
                   which complete actual data are not yet available) should include all actual data available at
                   that time.
                6. Wherever responses include estimated information, include an explanation (or reference to

         BY THE COMMISSION:

                 The Corporation Commission of the State of Oklahoma ("the Commission") being
         regularly in session and the undersigned Commissioners being present and participating, there
         comes on for consideration and action the above cause for an order by the Commission.

         PROCEDURAL HISTORY

                On December 12, 2002, Joyce E. Davidson, Director of the Public Utility Division for the
         Oklahoma Corporation Commission ("Staff") filed her Application for a review of the fuel
         adjustment clause of Public Service Company of Oklahoma ("PSO") for the year 2001. On
         January 3, 2003, the Attorney General entered an appearance in this Cause. On January 3, 2003,
         the Oklahoma Industrial Energy Consumers ("OIEC") filed its Motion to Intervene, which was
         granted by Order Number 471729. On July 8, 2003, PSO filed its Motion to Establish
         Procedural Schedule.
                On July 21, 2003, the Commission entered Order Number 478293, which was the Agreed
         Procedural Order establishing the dates for processing this Cause. Pursuant to Order Number
         478293, the hearing on the merits was set for October 7, 2003 at 9:30 a.m. On September 16,

         September 19, 2003, OIEC filed Objections to a majority of PSO’s Data Requests, but provided
         responses to those Data Requests to which OIEC did not object..„,
                 On February 12, 2004, the Administrative Law Judge Maribeth D. Snapp ("ALJ") filed
         her Report regarding the Objections of OIEC to certain Data Requests from PSO. In said report,
         the ALJ required that OIEC respond to and produce information relating to the following Data
         Requests from the First Set of Data Requests submitted by PSO: 1.6, 1.7, 1.13, 1.15, 1.16, 1.19,
         1.22, 1.23, 1.24, 1.27, 1.29 through 1.41, 1.43, 1.44, 1.47, 1.48, and 1.59. More particularly,
         OIEC was ordered to produce information from only the top seven OIEC companies, by gross
         revenue, related to the Data Requests numbered: 1.16, 1.19, 1.22, 1.23, 1.24, 1,27, 1.30 through
         1.41, and 1.44.
                 On February 23, 2004, PSO filed its Appeal to the ALJ’s February 12, 2004 Report in
         which it requested the Commission order all of OIEC's members to respond to these Data
         Requests and not just those top seven OIEC members. On February 23, 2004, OIEC also filed an
         Appeal to the ALJ’s February 12, 2004 ruling and propounded that the information sought, even
         as modified by the ALJ’s ruling, was not relevant to the proceedings in this cause.
                 On March 12, 2004, the Appeals were heard before the Commission, En Banc. After
         hearing the arguments of all parties, the Commission entered a unanimous ruling that the
         information requested in PSO’s First Data Requests at issue in this Appeal are not discoverable.

                IT IS THEREFORE THE ORDER OF THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE
